thread:
Maya: noticing a sustained increase in p95/p99 on /v1/generate in prod-us-east-1 around 14:05 UTC. p99 moved from ~1.0s to ~2.7s. customer CS-9411 reported timeouts.
Raj: can you post the route+model and a grafana link?
Maya: grafana: https://grafana.internal/d/abcd/inference-runtime?panel=route-latency... affected: /v1/generate model=redwood/fast-8k region=prod-us-east-1. spike aligns with deploy ~14:00 UTC.
deploy-bot: deploy completed: infra/deploy commit=6f9a2e (PR#4521) 2026-03-10T14:00:00Z by oliver
Oliver: that PR changed cache key logic to keep the 'raw' structured prompt intact and removed canonicalization. intended to preserve structured prompt fidelity.
Sara: CS says customers see p95/p99 regressions, some 504s. ticket #CS-9411. need ETA and mitigation.
Luis: digging logs for request ids from the ticket. observed prefix_cache_miss_rate jumped 0.03 -> 0.48 after deploy. kv_eviction_rate up too.
Maya: top metrics snapshot:
- p95 /v1/generate: 0.95s -> 1.8s
- p99 /v1/generate: 1.05s -> 2.7s
- prefix_cache_miss_rate: 0.03 -> 0.48
- kv_eviction_rate: 0.002 -> 0.15
- per-node CPU: +30% on prefix lookup hot nodes
Raj: likely cache cardinality explosion from high-granularity keys. any sampled keys?
Maya: grabbing debug sample from runtime cache logs. snippet:
```
[2026-03-10T14:02:21Z] prefix_cache_check key="conv=4217|prompt=Please summarize: Hello" miss
[2026-03-10T14:02:21Z] prefix_cache_check key="conv=4217|prompt=Please summarize:\\n" miss
[2026-03-10T14:02:21Z] prefix_cache_check key="conv=4217|prompt=Please summarize: hello" miss
[2026-03-10T14:02:21Z] prefix_cache_check key="conv=4217|prompt=Please summarize:\u00A0Hello" miss
```
Maya: variations include trailing newline, case, and non-breaking space. the canonicalization was removed in PR#4521 so tiny user-side differences create unique cache keys.
Oliver: confirmed. I removed KeyCanonicalizer.normalize() to preserve original tokens for exact structured-run identity. didn't realize the cache depended on that normalization.
Raj: that would explain the miss rate and eviction churn. every request misses and repopulates different keys, causing thrash.
Sara: immediate mitigation needed — customers affected during peak bursts.
Maya: proposed immediate playbook:
1) rollback PR#4521 via canary -> full region (low risk, known good)
2) short-term: add a lightweight cache-key pre-normalizer (strip/truncate/normalize unicode, lowercase) at cache ingress only
3) scale prefix cache capacity by +50% in prod-us-east while rollback is validated
4) add alerting for prefix_cache_miss_rate > 0.1 and cache_key_cardinality spike
5) schedule background cache warmup for top conversation ids
6) add unit + perf tests to PR gating
Oliver: opening rollback PR now, will deploy a 10% canary to us-east-1-a. infra rolling it out.
deploy-bot: canary deploy started: deploy-4521-rollback-canary id=deploy-4521-canary at 2026-03-10T14:12:00Z
Raj: watching canary dashboards. canary p99 back to ~1.2s within 90s; miss rate on canary nodes dropped to 0.02.
Maya: good signal. if canary holds for 10m, promote.
Oliver: canary healthy at 10m. promoting full rollback to prod-us-east.
deploy-bot: rollback deploy completed: deploy-4521-rollback full at 2026-03-10T14:25:00Z
Raj: post-rollback: p99 back to ~1.0-1.3s, prefix_cache_miss_rate down to baseline, eviction_rate back to normal.
Sara: updated CS ticket CS-9411 with incident summary and mitigation; customers asked for postmortem and ETA.
Maya: follow-ups (owners):
- ACTION-1: add unit tests for cache key contract; include normalization-preservation matrix (owner: Oliver)
- ACTION-2: add perf e2e that fuzzes prompt whitespace and case and asserts miss_rate < 0.05 (owner: Raj)
- ACTION-3: expose cache_key_cardinality metric and alert (owner: Maya)
- ACTION-4: implement a configurable cache-key canonicalizer with opt-out per flow (owner: Oliver + eng-runtime)
- ACTION-5: run a 24h warmup for top-1k conv ids after rollback (owner: infra)
- ACTION-6: write incident postmortem and customer note (owner: Maya)
Oliver: I'll also add a PR-linter rule to flag removal of normalize() in files that touch cache key formation.
Luis: CS sending customers a brief apology + ETA (postmortem in 48h) and asked if we can provide affected request IDs and timeframe.
Maya: repro steps for eng to validate locally:
- send two semantic-equivalent requests that differ only by trailing whitespace/case/unicode normal form
curl example:
```
curl -s -X POST https://prod-us-east-1.api.internal/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" \
  -d '{"conversation_id":"conv:4217","prompt":"Please summarize: Hello"}'
# then variation
curl -s -X POST https://prod-us-east-1.api.internal/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" \
  -d '{"conversation_id":"conv:4217","prompt":"Please summarize: Hello\\n"}'
```
- check runtime/debug logs for distinct cache keys and misses.
Sara: thanks team. I'll keep CS updated and mark ticket impacted->mitigated. please sync to postmortem doc when ready.
Maya: adding runbook note: if prefix_cache_miss_rate > 0.1 AND recent deploys in last 30m -> sample cache keys, consider canary rollback + pre-normalizer.
Raj: also add PR gating to detect changes to KeyCanonicalizer.* without tests.
Maya: closing thread; migrating action items to tracker. will post link to postmortem when finished. :white_check_mark:
